subject: general
question: Which Part of the Indian Constitution is known as ‘Magna Carta of India’?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Part III**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Part III containing Fundamental Rights (Articles 12 to 35) is described as the Magna Carta of India.
 
• Magna Carta is the Charter of rights issued by King John of England.
 
• It is the first written document on the Fundamental Rights of the citizens. 
 
• In this regard, the framers of the Constitution derived inspiration from the Constitution of the USA (i.e., the Bill of Rights).
 
• Part III contains a very long and comprehensive list of ‘justiciable’ Fundamental Rights.
 
• In fact, the Fundamental Rights in our Constitution are more elaborate than those found in the Constitution of any other country in the world, including the USA.
 
• The Fundamental Rights are guaranteed by the Constitution to all persons without any discrimination.
 
• The Fundamental Rights are meant for promoting the idea of political democracy.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 **Part**
 **Deals with**
 
 

 Part-IV
 Article 36 to 51 of the Indian Constitution is related to the Directive Principle of our State Policy.
 
 

 Part II
 Articles 5 to 11 of the Indian constitution are related to Citizenship
 
 

 Part VI
 Article 152 to Article 237 deal with State Government.
